summary: Research for the LaTeX-notes feature: .tex source parsing libraries, math-aware PDF extraction, math-aware chunking/retrieval, document-grounded MCQ generation, assessment science (IRT/BKT/FSRS), reference implementations, and local-model constraints. Grounded in Sage's actual code (extraction registry, chunking, retrieval tokenizer, learning/teach/mastery services, DB schema).

findings.conclusion: Best fit for structure extraction. MIT-licensed, actively maintained (677 commits, 3.0beta pre-release advertised on PyPI, docs on readthedocs), ZERO runtime dependencies, Python >=3.6, pure Python (any-platform, ARM64-safe). Provides latexwalker (brace/group-balanced token stream: sections, environments, commands) and latex2text (LaTeX -> unicode plain text). It is explicitly NOT a full TeX engine, which is exactly what a notes scanner needs. Unknown macros degrade gracefully (parsed as unknown nodes).

A full LaTeX interpreter written in Python (341 stars, 1062 commits) that builds an XML-DOM. More powerful but far heavier: it executes TeX semantics, so arbitrary user packages/macros can break it, and it is overkill for extracting sections/environments from personal notes. Not recommended as the primary dependency.

latex2sympy (augustt198) is ARCHIVED (May 2020, Python 2.7, ANTLR-based). Active fork latex2sympy2 (OrangeX4, 148 stars, 413 commits) converts LaTeX math to SymPy; requires sympy + antlr4-python3-runtime. Useful ONLY for symbolic canonicalization/equivalence checks of equations (e.g. verifying two options are the same expression), NOT for document structure. Overkill for v1; optionally later for answer verification.

texsoup repo could not be located/verified (404 on candidate URLs); it is a minor niche library with no clear maintenance story. A hand-rolled regex/state-machine scanner for \section and \begin{env}...\end{env} works for typical personal notes and is dependency-free, but breaks on comments (%), verbatim blocks, nested braces, and custom macros. Recommendation: use pylatexenc's latexwalker as the tokenizer underneath a small custom scanner (gets brace-balance + comments + macro awareness for free) rather than either extreme.
findings.source: no authoritative source found; inference from pylatexenc capabilities

findings.conclusion: PyMuPDF get_text returns the PDF text layer; for pdflatex-compiled PDFs this is often garbled or lossy for math: Computer Modern fonts without proper ToUnicode CMaps extract with wrong/missing glyphs, and even when glyphs map, the math layout (fractions, sums, spacing) is flattened or lost. Sage's own pdf.py already flags image-only pages. This is a recognized class of problem: MinerU's README advertises auto-detection of 'scanned PDFs and garbled PDFs' with OCR fallback precisely because text-layer math extraction is unreliable.
findings.source: https://github.com/opendatalab/MinerU (garbled-PDF detection feature); PyMuPDF behavior inferred from widely documented pdflatex/CM-font extraction issues

findings.topic: Math-aware PDF extraction: GROBID / MinerU / Marker / Nougat
findings.conclusion: All serious math-PDF extractors are heavyweight: GROBID is a Java service (OpenJDK 21, Apache 2.0, 5.1k stars, CRF by default, production-scale); MinerU is a PyTorch VLM+OCR pipeline (77.9k stars, multi-GB model downloads, CPU-capable but slow, custom Apache-based license); Marker/Nougat are similar transformer-based model pipelines needing GPU realistically. None is proportionate for a single-user, small-corpus, possibly-ARM64 tutor, and none recovers the exact source structure the way the .tex source does. Mathpix is a paid API (rejected: local-first requirement).

'Use the .tex source when available, PDF as fallback' is the right architecture: .tex gives lossless structure (sections, environments, equation labels) that no PDF pipeline can match, at zero ML cost. Matching .tex to .pdf by same basename in the same folder is feasible at upload time: the FileService stores raw bytes per file, so when a .tex and a .pdf with the same stem arrive, they can be paired; otherwise each is indexed independently. PDF without matching .tex: raw text-layer extraction WITH a warning (matches existing 'partial' status with warnings), not skip — the user can still get grounded Q&A, just with degraded math.
findings.source: codebase analysis: app/services/files.py (ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS, save_upload, warnings/partial status), app/services/extraction/pdf.py

findings.conclusion: The current tokenizer re _TOKEN_RE = r'[a-z0-9']+' drops every math symbol AND strips backslash commands: '\alpha' indexes as 'alpha', '\frac{a}{b}' as ['frac','a','b'], and unicode math chars from PDF extraction or user queries ('\u03b1', '\u222b') are dropped ENTIRELY (not just lowercased). So symbol-heavy queries ('\u222b x dx') and PDF-extracted unicode math are largely invisible to retrieval. Verified by direct code reading. A math-aware upgrade should: (1) keep LaTeX commands as tokens (e.g. '\alpha' or 'alpha'), (2) add unicode letter-like/symbol tokens (\w with unicode flag plus a symbol class), (3) canonicalize user \newcommand macros via a preamble map before tokenizing, and (4) index BOTH the raw-LaTeX rendering and a latex2text unicode rendering of each chunk.
findings.source: codebase analysis: app/services/retrieval.py tokenize(); pylatexenc latex2text for unicode rendering

findings.topic: Hybrid retrieval (BM25 + vectors) for small corpora
findings.conclusion: For a single-user corpus of a few MB, a math-aware lexical retriever is proportionate and strong: math notation is highly exact-match-friendly (\alpha, \int, theorem names are literal). Verified research support: arXiv:2607.06641 (RAG in public-health QA, 7,929 questions) shows hybrid retrieval consistently beats single-mode retrieval and that good retrieval lets small models match larger ones. A zero-dependency BM25 upgrade is available via SQLite FTS5 (bundled with CPython's sqlite3 since 3.8+; verify at runtime). Dense embeddings (sentence-transformers, e.g. all-MiniLM-L6-v2 ~22M params or e5 family) need torch (~400MB+ install, ARM64 wheels exist but slow on Pi); defer to a later milestone. Note: the local OpenAI-compatible endpoint's /embeddings availability is unverified — if present it would be the cheapest vector source.
findings.source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.06641 (Healthier LLMs: RAG for Public Health QA)

findings.conclusion: The strongest current pattern is knowledge-structure-driven generation: KNIGHT (arXiv:2602.20135, CPAL 2026) generates MCQs from an LLM-built knowledge graph and evaluates quality on exactly the right axes for Sage: fluency, unambiguity (single correct answer), topic relevance, option uniqueness, and answerability-given-sources (a hallucination proxy). A second paper (arXiv:2604.10748, Sakiroglu et al.) adds interpretable difficulty estimation and KG-sourced distractors. For Sage the proportionate application: use theorem/definition/example/lemma units as question seeds; instruct the model to write distractors as plausible near-misses (hypothesis swaps, misapplied conditions) and to make the correct option a verbatim-or-near source statement; add a cheap one-call verification pass re-asking whether the correct option is literally supported by the source block (answerability check). For provenance, extend the quiz_questions schema with a source_ref (chunk_id + section + environment + equation label) and echo it in the explanation.
findings.source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.20135 (KNIGHT); https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.10748 (MCQ generation with interpretable difficulty); codebase: app/llm/structured.py request_questions, app/services/learning.py

findings.topic: Assessment science: IRT vs BKT vs proportion vs FSRS
findings.conclusion: IRT needs item parameters and many responses per item — wrong for a single user with sparse data. BKT (hidden Markov mastery model) needs parameter fitting and per-skill response streams — also data-starved here. The current Laplace-smoothed proportion (mastery.py _laplace_confidence, (correct+1)/(observed+2)) is the right proportionate baseline for in-session mastery. For cross-session review scheduling, FSRS is published, open source, and directly usable: algorithm documented on the awesome-fsrs wiki, MIT-licensed reference implementations exist (fsrs4anki, 4k stars; Python ports in awesome-fsrs), academic grounding in Maimemo KDD 2022 / TKDE 2023 papers. It needs per-card review history (stability/difficulty/due dates), which maps to a future review_schedule table keyed by topic+note rather than the current global topic row; Sage's evidence_json already stores timestamps per observation, so the raw data for a later FSRS integration is already being collected.
findings.source: https://github.com/open-spaced-repetition/fsrs4anki (MIT, algorithm wiki, Maimemo papers); codebase: app/services/mastery.py

findings.topic: Reference implementations for the 1-on-1 tutor pattern
findings.conclusion: The pi agent harness (referenced in the task as having a 'teach' skill) is real but its canonical repo URL could not be verified directly (404s on candidate URLs); verified ecosystem evidence: c4pt0r/pie is a Rust port of the pi agent harness, omnigent-ai/omnigent (9k stars) orchestrates Pi among other agents, vastsa/PI-Desktop bundles it. Instructive open-source references worth studying for Sage's feature: (1) c4pt0r/pie (pi harness port — agent-with-skills pattern, incl. teach-style skills), (2) open-spaced-repetition/fsrs4anki + awesome-fsrs (spaced repetition scheduling), (3) grobidOrg/grobid (math-aware PDF structuring, for the fallback path's ambitions), (4) opendatalab/MinerU (formula-to-LaTeX extraction reference quality bar). Khanmigo/Mem/NotebookLM are instructive but closed-source — their published UX descriptions (grounding, citations) match what Sage already does with [DOC]/[cit:] blocks.
findings.confidence: verified (repos listed); pi canonical URL unverified

findings.topic: Model constraints: deepseek-v4-pro class local model
findings.conclusion: The existing complete_json/request_questions stack already handles the common structured-output failure modes: parse_json strips markdown fences and locates the first balanced JSON object/array, and structured.py retries with a repair prompt (PLAN_RETRY_NOTE / QUESTIONS_RETRY_NOTE). Math-heavy JSON has one specific pitfall: LaTeX backslashes inside JSON strings must be escaped ('\\alpha'), which local models often forget, producing invalid JSON; mitigations: prefer unicode math ('\u03b1', '\u222b') in question/option text, keep LaTeX only in the source blocks (data, not parsed), and rely on the existing retry path. Math explanation quality in plain prose is generally good for v4-pro-class models; long-context grounding is a non-issue at the current budget (8 chunks x 1500 chars ~= 12K chars << typical context windows). Vision/OCR is NOT needed for LaTeX-compiled PDFs that have a text layer; image-only PDFs are already handled with a warning by pdf.py. The 'deepseek-v4-pro' model name is the local endpoint alias (config.py brot_model); no external docs verified for it.
findings.source: codebase analysis: app/llm/structured.py (parse_json, retry notes), app/config.py; JSON/LaTeX escaping pitfall inferred from standard JSON semantics

recommendations: Add a .tex extractor via the existing @register('tex') framework in app/services/extraction/tex.py, built on pylatexenc's latexwalker (sole new runtime dep, zero-dependency, ARM64-safe). Emit units per section and per theorem/definition/example/lemma/proposition/corollary/proof/equation/align environment with LocationInfo(kind='section', section=..., start_line/end_line); also carry an equation label and a latex2text unicode rendering. Parse \newcommand/\def from the preamble into a macro map; skip preamble from units but store it (macro canonicalization + metadata).

Add '.tex' to ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS and _MIME_BY_EXT in files.py. At upload time, pair a .tex with a same-basename .pdf when both are present (store a pairing field or just rely on matching stems at ingest); index each independently otherwise.

PDF without a matching .tex: keep raw PyMuPDF text-layer extraction but surface a warning ('math may be garbled; upload the .tex source for lossless extraction') via the existing warnings/partial-status path. Do NOT integrate GROBID/MinerU/Marker/Nougat now; record them in oc-wants.txt as a possible later milestone. Do not add OCR in v1.

Math-aware retrieval: upgrade the tokenizer so LaTeX commands and unicode math survive (keep r'[a-z0-9\']+' tokens AND add \\[a-zA-Z]+ command tokens and unicode letter/symbol tokens), canonicalize user macros via the preamble map, and index a second latex2text unicode rendering alongside raw LaTeX. Consider SQLite FTS5 (built-in) for proper BM25 ranking as a zero-dependency improvement; defer dense embeddings (torch/sentence-transformers) to a later milestone — for a few-MB corpus, math-aware lexical retrieval is proportionate and math is exact-match friendly.

Chunking: keep the 1500/200 char window but make the .tex extractor emit environment-scoped units so boundaries never split inside a theorem/equation; treat oversize environments as the only intra-unit split case, snapping at blank lines outside display-math spans.

Document-grounded quizzes: add a notes-quiz mode that seeds questions from theorem/definition/example units, with prompt guidance encoding KNIGHT's quality criteria (unambiguity, answerability from source, near-miss distractors); add a single verification call that checks the correct option is literally supported by the source block; extend quiz_questions with a source_ref column (chunk_id + section + environment + label) surfaced in explanations. A schema migration (SCHEMA_VERSION 1 -> 2 in db.py) is required.

Assessment: keep Laplace-smoothed proportion as the mastery model for now (proportionate, already implemented); do NOT implement IRT/BKT (data too sparse for one user). When cross-session review scheduling is wanted, adopt the published, MIT-licensed FSRS algorithm with a review_schedule table keyed by topic+note; evidence_json already accumulates the timestamps needed.

Model constraints: keep LaTeX in source blocks only; emit question/option text in unicode math to dodge JSON backslash-escaping failures; keep relying on the existing fence-stripping parse_json + retry notes. No vision capability needed for LaTeX-compiled PDFs.
